It's interesting to consider the historical evolution of our understanding of the universe.

Go back hundreds to thousands of years back and we viewed the universe as something described and defined by religion. The sun (and all the universe) rotated around a flat Earth which was God's chosen place for his special people. This was all proven by basic science to be wrong. In fact we're relatively nondescript spherical planet orbiting about a nondescript star in a nondescript section of a nondescript galaxy in a universe with a countless number of other planets, stars, and even galaxies. No, the universe is most certainly not as described by any human religion.

So we assumed everything was logical. It was defined not by god, but by simple intuitive logic. And by the early 20th century many scientists thought physics and such science was getting close to being 'done.' Then came in relativity. Now suddenly in comes to be that time is itself just another dimension of 'movement' that can be traversed at different rates for different individuals and was no longer a universal constant. Something that is about as inhumanly illogical as you can possibly get. And then about the same time as relativity, we start to really dig into quantum mechanics and start to notice the world on a small scale gets even more ridiculous with seemingly 'magical' connections, particles behaving differently when observed than when not observed, and all other sorts of other completely ridiculous discoveries. No the universe is certainly not just a place of intuitive logic.

So back to the present now we know enough to know we know nothing. There's a gaping maw between our understanding of the universe at the big scale and the small scale. String theory is an attempt to ultimately bridge this gap while also assimilating everything we know and tying it all together. It's not unsubstantial. It's already also offering some predictions such as supersymmetry. And there are various means to work to try to verify other predictions (or precepts I suppose) of string theory such as additional dimensions. The point of string theory is that for now it seems be the key fitting the keyhole that is our universe most accurately with hopes that it'll help us turn the lock a bit more than we have been able to in the past with our present disconnected attempts.
